transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Patel, Miguel Torres, Sara Lim, Evan Brooks, Tom Rivera, Jenna Kline, Liam O'Neill, Nina Park

Summary: Quick run through launch readiness, incident postmortem follow-up, canary plan and monitoring updates.

[00:00] Alex Chen: ok, thanks everyone for joining, i'll kick us off. we've got a packed agenda, uh, mostly launch readiness items and the incident follow up from the 12th. can we do a quick round of who has blockers?

[00:22] Priya Patel: yeah, hi everyone, Priya here. blockers mostly around the canary config, specifically the routing policy and the fallback thresholds, i want to make sure we don't end up thundering herd on the ded- or on the dedicated pool when we failover. also we need a clear mttd/mttr on the rollback path.

[00:45] Miguel Torres: SRE side, the KV cache warmup is still flaky in staging, i think it's a timing issue with cache priming and the earliest tokens for long conversations; sometimes the cold start latency spikes. we saw that in the 10-12 incident as well.

[01:05] Sara Lim: product check, we need to confirm the feature gates and API versioning aligned, some internal sdks are still referencing old param names. Alex, are we confident the sdks will be pushed before freeze?

[01:22] Alex Chen: good point. SDK team said they'd have the patch by Friday, but i asked them to triage priority; i'll follow up right after this.

[01:35] Jenna Kline: QA has one test failing intermittently around rate limit backoff, it's probably a test timing flakiness but want to flag it now so it doesn't block the rehearsal.

[01:50] Tom Rivera: for context, leadership wants a clear go/no-go criteria: critical SLOs within tolerance, successful canary with <2% error and no data loss, and rehearsal success. if any of those fail we push.

[02:15] Nina Park: timing items - freeze non-critical changes on 2026-10-25, rehearsal 2026-10-26, launch window target 2026-10-28. please confirm availability for rehearsal.

[02:35] Alex Chen: noted. let's go into the incident review from 10-12 - Miguel, can you walk us through the timeline?

[02:45] Miguel Torres: yeah, so timeline, approx 03:10 UTC we started to see increased latencies on the hosted cluster, the root cause traced to a misconfigured autoscaler policy combined with a post-deploy spike in KV fetches, which overloaded the GPU inference pool and triggered cascading queue growth. essentially a combination of config drift and an unexpected traffic pattern from an internal job.

[03:25] Priya Patel: just to clarify, was it a model-specific pattern or infra-level? was the attention kernel causing resource contention?

[03:35] Miguel Torres: it looked infra-level - the model kernels were fine, but the queue growth came from long-running open conversations that caused large KV caches to be read and those reads serialized on a small number of serving nodes.

[03:50] Liam O'Neill: I want to flag the internal job - the nightly indexing job fired earlier than scheduled due to clock drift on one of the cron runners; that amplified load during the deploy. we've already patched the cron guards.

[04:05] Evan Brooks: QA saw that think time between requests was lower in that window, so our load generation didn't replicate it; we'll update the load tests to include bursty conversational patterns with large state sizes.

[04:25] Alex Chen: ok, so actionable items from the postmortem - tighten autoscaler policies, enforce cron guards, improve KV cache priming and add eviction pre-warm, and update load tests. Miguel, can you own the runbook updates?

[04:38] Miguel Torres: yes, I'll own runbook changes and the rollback procedures. I'll add explicit steps for rollback, and a pre-hotstart KV priming script.

[05:00] Jenna Kline: adding on, QA will add degraded-network and cache-thrashing scenarios. I'll attach the failing logs to the ticket.

[05:15] Alex Chen: good. moving to canary rollout plan - Priya, walk us through the proposed gating metrics.

[05:25] Priya Patel: plan is phased canary: 1% initial traffic for 2 hours, then 5% for 4 hours if SLOs hold, then 20% for 6 hours, then ramp to full. gating metrics: p95 latency, token-level error rates, OOMs, and tail latency spikes. threshold: p95 within 15% of baseline, error rate <0.5% and no persistent OOMs or GPU saturations.

[06:05] Sara Lim: do we have automated rollback triggers? I'd prefer we auto-roll back on sustained p95 >20% or error rate >0.8% for more than 5 minutes.

[06:20] Priya Patel: yes, we can set those as automated triggers but keep a manual override. we'll also include a human-in-the-loop notification to oncall.

[06:35] Miguel Torres: note: auto-rollback must also ensure the KV cache isn't left in inconsistent state; we'll add a step to clear partial caches or redirect to safe variant.

[06:50] Alex Chen: sounds good. Evan, status on load testing and stress scenarios?

[07:00] Evan Brooks: running the 10k rps profile today, baseline pass earlier but need to add bursty long-convo patterns; expect final results tomorrow. I've got a flaky test to debug around backoff, but that's on my plate.

[07:20] Nina Park: docs - where are we on the runbook visibility? we need a single doc in confluence with owners and rollback checklist.

[07:32] Miguel Torres: I'll create the runbook page and link to the automated playbooks; will assign owners.

[07:45] Alex Chen: ok also there's an API versioning note - SDK breaks possible; I'll confirm with SDK team that patch is out. if not, we delay.

[08:00] Priya Patel: also, dedicated vs hosted routing - we need final decision for canary: route canary traffic to hosted first or to a mixed pool? suggestion is hosted-only for initial small percent to reduce customer impact.

[08:18] Tom Rivera: hosted-only sounds safer, we can avoid touching dedicated reserved pools until after canary signals green.

[08:30] Sara Lim: agreed. also reminder: update user-facing docs to mention feature opt-in and rate limits.

[08:42] Alex Chen: good. next, monitoring threshold adjustments - Miguel, what changes do you propose?

[08:50] Miguel Torres: increase granularity on GPU utilization alerts, add token-rate based alerting, and set a p99 token latency alert with 1-minute burn rate. also add synthetic traces for long conversation scenarios.

[09:10] Evan Brooks: we'll integrate those into the dashboard and the rehearsal checklist. I'll own dashboard updates.

[09:25] Jenna Kline: QA will validate alerts trigger appropriately; I'll include alert-firing scenarios in the rehearsal.

[09:40] Alex Chen: ok we're approaching the last 10 minutes, quick round: any other risks?

[09:50] Priya Patel: risk: rolling back causes partial cache invalidation that spikes cold-start latency; mitigation: add staggered rollback and pre-warm on a small pool.

[10:05] Miguel Torres: also risk: autoscaler misconfig on edge cases, we should do a dry-run in staging with the autoscaler policies.

[10:18] Nina Park: logistic risk: make sure all stakeholders can attend the rehearsal on the 26th; I'll send the calendar invite and follow up.

[10:30] Alex Chen: recap and next steps: freeze non-critical changes 10-25, rehearsal 10-26, final go/no-go on 10-27, launch 10-28. Priya finalize canary, Miguel update runbooks, Evan finish load tests, Jenna expand QA scenarios, Nina schedule rehearsal.

[10:55] Tom Rivera: thanks all, leadership satisfied with plan if actions complete; please escalate any blockers early.

[11:05] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, i'll send the updated checklist and action items after this call. meeting adjourned.
